title: Moving timekeeping to the top cymbal; Jo Jones and Basie
summary: He rejected the sock-cymbal style of Jo Jones, studied it by following Basie, and moved to the ride cymbal to free his left hand and coordinate hands and feet.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: So I changed -- everyone wanted me to play like Joe Jones. But I didn't want to play like that.
No.
And I changed over to the top cymbal, which gave me the freedom of my left hand.
Yeah.
See, because Joe, he was cramped.
Yeah.

And I used to watch him. I used to follow Basie all over, to find out the advantage of playing the sock cymbal with the right hand like that, and I travelled all over the country with Basie, and sometimes would play in Joe's place, you know, to try to understand exactly --
Yeah.
But Joe, I don't know, I guess he had played that way so long that he had it quite undercover, exactly
what he wanted to do. But what he was doing had no bearing at all on what I wanted to do.
No.
I wanted to do something completely different.
Yeah.
And so I started playing this way, and freeing my left hand.
Yeah. So you became more ambidextrous.
That's right.
Yeah.
Because sometimes I would play and my idea was to never leave your left hand idle.
Yeah.

Because if people look up and they see me playing with one hand and this hand isn't doing anything, it's like a one handed piano player. So I said, well, I can't be one handed. I have to learn to play with this other hand.
Yeah.
So I began to work on it, to coordinate with my right foot.
Your left hand and your right foot?
And right foot. And my right hand with my left foot.
Gee.

You know, because rinky-dink, bang, I had the sock cymbal over here, and the left hand was the bass drum, so I figured, I said -- and I talked to Diz about it, and he said, "That's a perfect combination." Said, "Now you have the whole thing working." So then I began to work on it.
Well, so did you have drummers standing out there with their mouths open?
